subject: phy
title: Work, Energy and Power
syllabus: Work done by a constant force and a variable force; kinetic and potential energies, work-energy theorem, power. The potential energy of spring conservation of mechanical energy, conservative and non-conservative forces; motion in a vertical circle: Elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions.

topics.work: Work done by constant and variable forces
topics.cons: Potential energy, springs & conservation of energy

body: Constant force: W = F⃗ · d⃗ = Fd cosθ. Positive when the force helps the motion, negative when it opposes, zero when perpendicular.
Variable force: W = ∫F dx = area under the F–x graph
Gravity and springs are conservative: their work depends only on the end points (mgh, ½kx^{2}). Friction is not: W = μN × path length.

check.why: 6 − 6 = 0: the force is perpendicular to the motion.

body: K = ½mv^{2} = \f{p^{2}}{2m}. Same momentum → the lighter body has more KE. K × n → p × √{n}.
W_{net} = ΔK (work by ALL forces)
Projectile: at the top only u cosθ remains → K_{top} = K cos^{2}θ.
Bullet through a plank: fraction of KE lost = 1 − (\f{v}{u})^{2}.
P = \f{dW}{dt} = F⃗ · v⃗. Average power = \f{total work}{time}.
Time-dependent force from rest: integrate a = F/m to get v⃗, then P = F⃗ · v⃗.
Constant power from rest: ½mv^{2} = Pt → v ∝ t^{1/2}, x ∝ t^{3/2}.
Constant force from rest: instantaneous P grows as t, so P_{avg} = ½P_{final}.

body: U_{gravity} = mgh; U_{spring} = ½kx^{2}. Force = −\f{dU}{dx}.
No friction: K + U = constant
Hanging spring in equilibrium: x = \f{mg}{k}, U = \f{(mg)^{2}}{2k}. Cutting a spring: k × length stays constant.
Loop of radius R: just making the top needs h = 2.5R; if the track pushes with nmg at the top, h = 2R + \f{(n + 1)R}{2}.

body: Momentum is conserved in every collision; KE only in elastic ones.
e = \f{speed of separation}{speed of approach}; e = 1 elastic, e = 0 sticks together
Elastic, target at rest: v_{1} = \f{m_{1} − m_{2}}{m_{1} + m_{2}}u, v_{2} = \f{2m_{1}}{m_{1} + m_{2}}u. Equal masses swap velocities.
Bounce with restitution e: rebound height = e^{2}h. Gun recoil: \f{K_{gun}}{K_{bullet}} = \f{m}{M}.

traps: Work against gravity is mgh whatever the path — a ramp only spreads it over a longer distance.
The work–energy theorem uses the work of ALL forces, including friction.
Same momentum does NOT mean same KE: K = p²/2m.
In an inelastic collision momentum is still conserved — only KE is lost.
For a hanging spring, the extra pull-down adds to the stretch already present: U_max uses the total stretch.
Cutting a spring makes each piece STIFFER, not softer.

steps.note: Springs, loops, elastic and inelastic collisions

pyq.q: A body of mass 50 kg is lifted to a height of 20 m from the ground in two different ways: Case 1 — pulled straight up; Case 2 — pushed along a smooth ramp inclined at 30°. The ratio of work done against gravity in the two cases will be :
sol: Work against gravity = mgh depends only on the height gained, not the path.
Ramp: force mg sin30° × length 40 m = mg × 20 → same → 1 : 1.

pyq.q: A force (3x^{2} + 2x − 5) N displaces a body from x = 2 m to x = 4 m. Work done by this force is ____ J.
A force F⃗ = 2î + bĵ + k̂ is applied on a particle and it undergoes a displacement î − 2ĵ − k̂. What will be the value of b, if work done on the particle is zero.
A block of mass 100 kg slides over a distance of 10 m on a horizontal surface. If the co-efficient of friction between the surfaces is 0.4, then the work done against friction (in J) is :
A 1 kg block subjected to two simultaneous forces (2î + 3ĵ + 4k̂) N and (3î − ĵ − 2k̂) N is moved a distance of 25 m along (3î − 4ĵ) direction. The work done in this process is ____ J.

A block of mass 1 kg is pushed up a surface inclined to horizontal at an angle of 60° by a force of 10 N parallel to the inclined surface. The coefficient of friction is 0.1. When the block is pushed up by 10 m along the inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is : [g = 10 m/s^{2}]
A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time t is proportional to :
An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force F⃗ = (2tî + 3t^{2}ĵ) N. The power generated by the force at time t is:
sol: Starting from rest, m = 1 kg: v⃗ = t^{2}î + t^{3}ĵ.

pyq.q: A body of mass 2 kg begins to move under the influence of time dependent force F⃗ = (2tî + 6t^{2}ĵ) N. The power produced by the force at t = 2 s is ____ W.
A body of mass 2 kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by F⃗ = (6tî + 6t^{2}ĵ) N. The power developed by the force at the time t is given by:

If a rubber ball falls from a height h and rebounds upto the height of h/2. The percentage loss of total energy of the initial system as well as velocity ball before it strikes the ground, respectively, are :
sol: Energy mgh → mg\f{h}{2}: half is lost → 50%.

pyq.q: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be :
A bullet of mass 50 g is fired with a speed 100 m/s on a plywood and emerges with 40 m/s. The percentage loss of kinetic energy is :
Four particles A, B, C, D of mass \f{m}{2}, m, 2m, 4m, have same momentum, respectively. The particle with maximum kinetic energy is :
sol: K = \f{p^{2}}{2m}: same p → the lightest has the most KE.

pyq.q: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along x-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by x(t) = αt^{2} + βt + γ m, where α = 1 m/s^{2}, β = 1 m/s and γ = 1 m. The work done on the body during the time interval t = 2 s to t = 3 s, is ……… J.
sol: v = 2αt + β = 2t + 1 → 5 m/s at 2 s, 7 m/s at 3 s.

pyq.q: A ball of mass 100 g is projected with velocity 20 m/s at 60° with horizontal. The decrease in kinetic energy of the ball during the motion from point of projection to highest point is
sol: At the top only the horizontal part u cos60° = 10 m/s remains.

pyq.q: A ball having kinetic energy KE, is projected at an angle of 60° from the horizontal. What will be the kinetic energy of ball at the highest point of its flight ?
sol: At the top v = u cos60° = \f{u}{2}.

pyq.q: An object is projected with kinetic energy K from a point A at an angle 60° with the horizontal. B is the highest point and C is where it lands at the same level as A. The ratio of the difference in kinetic energies at points B and C to that at point A (in the absence of air friction) is :
sol: K_{B} = K cos^{2}60° = \f{K}{4}; K_{C} = K (same level).

pyq.q: A body of mass 1 kg moves along a straight line with a velocity v = 2x^{2} (starting from rest at x = 0). The work done by the net force on the body during displacement from x = 0 to 5 m is ____ J.
sol: Work–energy: W = ½mv^{2} at x = 5 (v = 50 m/s).

pyq.q: A particle is released from height S above the surface of the earth. At certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of the earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively.
sol: K = 3U and K + U = mgS → U = \f{mgS}{4} → h = \f{S}{4}.

pyq.q: A block of mass 2 kg is attached to one end of a massless spring whose other end is fixed at a wall. The spring-mass system moves on a frictionless horizontal table. The spring's natural length is 2 m and spring constant is 200 N/m. The block is pushed such that the length of the spring becomes 1 m and then released. At distance x m (x < 2) from the wall, the speed of the block will be
A massless spring gets elongated by amount x_{1} under a tension of 5 N. Its elongation is x_{2} under the tension of 7 N. For the elongation of (5x_{1} − 2x_{2}), the tension in the spring will be,

A bead of mass 'm' slides without friction on the wall of a vertical circular hoop of radius 'R'. The bead moves under the combined action of gravity and a massless spring (k) attached to the bottom of the hoop. The equilibrium length of the spring is 'R'. If the bead is released from top of the hoop with (negligible) zero initial speed, velocity of bead, when the length of spring becomes 'R', would be (spring constant is 'k', g is acceleration due to gravity)
sol: Top: spring length 2R, stretch R. Chord R from the bottom → the bead is R(1 − cos60°) = \f{R}{2} above the bottom.

pyq.q: Two blocks with masses 100 g and 200 g are hung in equilibrium from the ends of springs A and B respectively. The energy stored in A is E. The energy stored in B, when spring constants k_{A}, k_{B} of A and B, respectively satisfy the relation 4k_{A} = 3k_{B}, is :
A spring of force constant 15 N/m is cut into two pieces. If the ratio of their length is 1 : 3, then the force constant of smaller piece is ____ N/m.
sol: k ∝ \f{1}{length}: the smaller piece is \f{1}{4} of the spring.

pyq.q: A spring stretches by 2 mm when it is loaded with a mass of 200 g. From equilibrium position the mass is further pulled down by 2 mm and released. The frequency associated with the system and maximum energy in the spring are ____ Hz and ____ J, respectively. (Take g = 10 m/s^{2})

A body of m kg slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point A to B in friction less path. A is on the upper half, its radius making 45° with the upward vertical; B is the lowest point. The velocity of the body at B is : (given, R = 14 m, g = 10 m/s^{2} and √{2} = 1.4)
sol: Drop from A to B = R + R cos45° = 14 + 9.8 = 23.8 m.

pyq.q: A smooth inclined plane ends in a vertical circular loop of radius R. A small body is released from height h. If the body exerts a force of three times its weight on the plane at the highest point of circle then the height h = αR. The value of α is ____ .
sol: At the top: N + mg = \f{mv^{2}}{R} with N = 3mg → v^{2} = 4gR.

pyq.q: An artillery piece of mass M_{1} fires a shell of mass M_{2} horizontally. Instantaneously after the firing, the ratio of kinetic energy of the artillery and that of the shell is

A body starts falling freely from height H and hits an inclined plane in its path at height h. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of \f{H}{h} for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is ____.
sol: Time = √{\f{2(H − h)}{g}} + √{\f{2h}{g}} (after the bounce the vertical speed is zero).

pyq.q: A small bob A of mass m is attached to a massless rigid rod of length 1 m pivoted at point P and kept at an angle of 60° with vertical. At distance of 1 m below point P, an identical bob B is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius R. If bob B just manages to complete the circular path of radius R after being hit elastically by bob A, then radius R is ____ m. (g = 10 m/s^{2})
sol: Equal masses, elastic → B gets v^{2} = 10. Just completing: v^{2} = 5gR → R = \f{10}{50} = \f{1}{5} m.

pyq.q: In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses 15 kg and 25 kg, moving in opposite directions with speeds of 10 m/s and 30 m/s, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in °C), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is : (specific heat of sphere material 31 cal/kg °C and 1 cal = 4.2 J)

Bob A of a pendulum having massless string of length 'R' is released from 60° to the vertical. It hits another bob B of half the mass that is at rest on a frictionless table in the center. Assuming elastic collision, the magnitude of the velocity of bob A after the collision will be (take g as acceleration due to gravity.)

Assertion (A): Three identical spheres A, B, C (in that order) move along one line with velocities v_{A} = 5 m/s, v_{B} = 2 m/s, v_{C} = 4 m/s. If we wait sufficiently long for elastic collisions to happen, then v_{A} = 4 m/s, v_{B} = 2 m/s, v_{C} = 5 m/s will be the final velocities. Reason (R): In an elastic collision between identical masses, two objects exchange their velocities. Choose the correct answer :
sol: Equal masses, elastic → velocities swap (R true).
A hits B: A 2, B 5. B hits C: B 4, C 5. Then A 2 < B 4 < C 5 — no more collisions.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
